source.scope: Ten existing non-mutating registered-tool T01 cases, revised after independent source review. Procedures only; no case executed and no test status changed.

build_profile_reload: Follow the full resource/build/reload preflight in docs/stabilization/PLAN.md. Use a current imported development artifact selected from its receipt set, not a directory name. Confirm ci-receipt.json, provenance.json, import-status.json, local-dev-receipt.json agree on source SHA, run/attempt, artifact ID/digest, extension version/ID and tree hash; compare the loaded chrome-mv3 tree to local-dev-receipt.json. Stop if identity or hash differs.

Before assertions, record chrome://version profile path and chrome://extensions extension ID/version/Loaded from path. Load the exact receipt-bound chrome-mv3 folder if needed, reload the extension, close/reopen the side panel, then reload the selected target tab. Keep each case unverified until actually run against that artifact.
manual_surface: Use an existing signed-in member profile and repeat in an existing signed-in admin profile; do not change account roles. In Tools, find the named tool, expand its argument form, enter the case JSON, select Run, and inspect the inline result. This is a one-tool, user-initiated local run.

ToolsView.tsx says the manual Run skips the permission gate. Therefore these procedures verify manual handler behavior only; they do not verify dispatcher Ask/Act authorization or prove that a withheld Chrome permission is enforced. Do not remove permissions to manufacture a denial. Any permission refusal observed in normal operation is reportable, but is not a required negative test here.

Use a dedicated disposable Chrome profile containing only public targets and synthetic bookmarks/history for the browser-data cases. Never inspect or report the user's ordinary bookmarks or browsing history. Public page reads are read-only; do not submit forms or copy arbitrary page content into reports.
shared_setup.fixture: For page tools, use the public https://example.org/ page (title and visible heading provide stable public text) as the basic read-only target. For find/get_element_details, first run read_page and use one of its returned ref values. For reproducible browser-data results, prepare an isolated test profile with a small known set of bookmarks to public example.org URLs and visits to those same URLs; record only these public URLs and the isolated profile identifier. Do not seed or inspect the everyday profile.

EXT-F-4022-T01.title: Read visible controls and text from a public page
preconditions: Complete shared receipt-bound build/profile/reload setup.
Open public https://example.org/ in the active tab and confirm it is fully loaded; use no logged-in or personal page.
Warm/reload repetition: Run once on the warm loaded page; then reload extension, panel, and same target tab and rerun both filter calls.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
In Tools, open read_page and run with {"filter":"all","include_text":true,"include_bounds":false,"max_nodes":200}.

Inspect the inline result for the active page title/URL and returned element roles, names/text, and refs. Confirm the visible heading text appears; do not enable lazy-load or hidden-element collection for this baseline.
Run again with {"filter":"interactive","include_text":true,"max_nodes":200} and compare the returned elements.

After this warm pass, reload the extension, close/reopen Tools, and reload the same public tab. Repeat both read_page calls and apply the same heading/filter checks; compare visible content rather than refs.
expected: The all-elements result includes visible page content and element metadata, including the public heading; the interactive result contains only interactive elements. Visible page text and navigation remain unchanged. read_page clears/reapplies data-matrx-ref attributes in the DOM, so this is a visible-content-preserving read with a DOM metadata side effect.
If the tab is unsupported or scripting access is unavailable, the tool returns a visible refusal/error; do not count an empty/error result as a successful content read.
EXT-F-4022-T01.auth_notes: Inventory says guest is not applicable because Tools requires sign-in. Member/admin are applicable. Manual Run bypasses dispatcher authorization; this case does not cover Ask/Act.
limits: Exact node count and refs can vary with page/browser rendering; assert visible heading and role/filter behavior, not a fixed whole-page scrape.
The handler removes stale data-matrx-ref attributes and stamps current refs; do not describe the call as causing zero DOM mutation.

EXT-F-4023-T01.title: Find a known heading on the active public page before and after reload
preconditions: Complete shared setup; active tab is loaded https://example.org/.
Confirm the visible page heading before using its text as the search query.

A preceding read_page call on the active tab must return a candidate ref for the visible heading. Preserve that candidate evidence for checking find output; AI availability is required for this positive result path.

Warm/reload repetition: Warm run: acquire the heading candidate with read_page before find. Reload extension, panel, and target tab; reacquire a fresh candidate with read_page before the second find run.
steps: Warm execution: perform this sequence once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline results.
In Tools, run read_page on the active public target with {"filter":"all","include_text":true,"max_nodes":200}; record the returned ref and candidate text/role for the visible Example Domain heading.

In Tools, run find with {"query":"Example Domain","include_content":true,"limit":5}. Compare returned match refs against the current read_page candidate refs and check the matched candidate text/role is the visible heading.

Inspect used_cache and mode. A successful positive case requires a returned match whose ref is among current candidates and whose candidate text/role identifies the heading; a refusal, unavailable AI, missing match, or invented/unknown ref is not a pass.

For the separate reloaded run, reload the extension, close/reopen Tools, and reload the public tab. Run read_page again to reacquire the current heading candidate/ref, then repeat the same find query and candidate/ref/text check.
expected: For both warm and reloaded runs, find returns a match tied to a current read_page candidate ref whose candidate text/role identifies the visible Example Domain heading. Require the specific known match; any nonempty match list is insufficient.

If AI is unavailable/refuses, the expected result is an explicit unsuccessful/unverified run, not a pass. Do not assert an empty result for arbitrary no-match text: source sends zero-score candidates to AI, which can select one.
EXT-F-4023-T01.auth_notes: Member/admin applicable; guest not applicable at Tools surface. Manual execution does not exercise the dispatcher gate.
limits: AI-backed ranking can vary. The pass oracle is specifically a returned current candidate ref mapped to the visible known heading; record model refusal or a wrong/unknown ref as non-pass.

EXT-F-4027-T01.title: Capture structured data from the assigned active page
preconditions: Complete shared setup; with the Tools panel open, leave https://example.org/ as the active browser tab. Confirm its title and URL.
Warm/reload repetition: Run shallow/deep on the warm loaded target. Reload extension, panel, and target tab before repeating both captures.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
In Tools, open read_active_page and run with {} (deep defaults to false).
Inspect the inline SoupResult for url, capturedAt, metadata, article fields (title/content/excerpt), and arrays such as links/images; do not describe it as a concise summary.
Run {"deep":true}; this requests scrollToLoadLazy before capture. Verify it still captures the same public URL and valid structured fields, without requiring output to differ from shallow mode.
After extension and target reload, repeat the shallow and deep calls and check the same required structured fields and URL.
expected: Both successful calls return a structured SoupResult for the same public URL, including url, capturedAt, metadata, article, and media/link/structured-data collections as defined by SoupResult. The deep=true call first requests a bounded lazy-load scroll; identical shallow/deep content is acceptable.
Blocked Chrome pages, no active assigned tab, or capture failures return an explicit refusal/error; these do not count as a successful capture.
EXT-F-4027-T01.auth_notes: Inventory applicability is member/admin only. Tools manual run targets the focused tab and skips dispatcher permission checks; this is not proof of per-turn assigned-tab behavior.
limits: Do not expect a summary string or require deep output to differ. Lazy-loaded content and collection sizes vary by page/runtime.

EXT-F-4035-T01.title: Inspect a page element using a fresh read_page reference
preconditions: Complete shared setup; active target is https://example.org/ and contains no private or credential fields.
Warm/reload repetition: Run on the warm loaded target. After extension, panel, and target reload, reacquire the heading ref with read_page; never reuse the old ref.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
Run read_page with {"filter":"all","include_text":true,"max_nodes":200}.
Choose the returned ref attached to the visible Example Domain heading and copy that exact ref into get_element_details; do not invent a selector or reuse a ref after navigation.
Run get_element_details with {"ref":"<returned-ref>","include_html":false,"include_styles":false} and inspect the result.
After extension and target reload, run read_page again to obtain a fresh heading ref, then rerun get_element_details using only that newly returned ref.
expected: The result identifies the heading tag/text, attributes, bounding rectangle, visible=true, and child count. HTML/styles are not requested. This is an inspection; read_page may stamp data-matrx-ref attributes, but the visible page content is unchanged.
If the ref is absent/stale, an explicit no-element result is a failed setup for this positive case; reload the public target and create a fresh ref before retrying.
EXT-F-4035-T01.auth_notes: Member/admin applicable, guest not applicable at Tools. Catalog permission list is empty for this handler; manual run still does not establish any dispatcher permission behavior.
limits: Ref identifiers and coordinates vary per page load/window size. The input schema's tab_id representation should be checked against the current live catalog/handler before execution; this procedure omits it and relies on the active tab.

EXT-F-4036-T01.title: List loaded tabs and filter to a public target
preconditions: Complete shared setup in the disposable profile. Open https://example.org/ and one other public tab; no personal tabs should be present.
Warm/reload repetition: Run on the warm disposable profile. After extension/panel and both target-tab reloads, repeat both tab-list calls.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
Run list_open_tabs with {"all_windows":true,"loaded_only":true}.
Verify the result contains the two known public tabs and note count, titles, URLs, status, and active flag.
Run {"all_windows":true,"url":"https://example.org/*","loaded_only":true} and inspect the filtered result.
After this warm pass, reload the extension, close/reopen Tools, and reload both known public tabs. Repeat both list_open_tabs queries and check the same target-membership/filter criteria.
expected: The first result includes loaded tabs in the profile and count equals the returned tabs array length. The URL-filtered call includes the matching example.org tab and excludes the other target. The tool does not open, close, or modify tabs.
If Chrome URL matching semantics or a wildcard differs, record actual filter behavior as a catalog/handler mismatch rather than asserting a guessed match.
EXT-F-4036-T01.auth_notes: Inventory lists tabs permission; member/admin applicable. Manual Run bypasses permission gate, so no permission-denial result can be required here.
limits: Tab IDs/order/status may vary; only assert known targets, count consistency, and documented filters.

EXT-F-4037-T01.title: Read the tab-group list, including the empty state
preconditions: Complete shared setup in a disposable Chrome profile. If a group already exists, record its displayed title/color and one member tab; do not change group state.
Warm/reload repetition: Run on the warm disposable Chrome profile, then after extension reload and Tools reopen repeat the group query and visible group comparison.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
Run get_tab_groups with {}.

Inspect count and groups. If the isolated profile already has a group, compare its id/title/color/collapsed/window_id/tab_ids with Chrome's visible group and tabs. If there are no groups, record the empty state.
After this warm pass, reload the extension and reopen Tools, then run get_tab_groups again and compare the current visible Chrome groups using the same count/membership criteria.
expected: On supported Chrome, result contains count equal to groups array length; each reported tab_ids entry belongs to that group. Zero groups is a valid observed empty state.
If chrome.tabGroups is unavailable, handler returns {ok:false,reason:'tabGroups API unavailable'}; report browser capability mismatch, not a successful empty result.
EXT-F-4037-T01.auth_notes: Inventory lists tabs and tabGroups permissions; handler advertises Chrome support only. Member/admin applicable. Manual run does not exercise authorization gate.
limits: No group is created or edited by this procedure. Current catalog permission declarations should be reconciled with Chrome's effective capability before claiming a gate result.

EXT-F-4038-T01.title: Look up details for a known open public tab
preconditions: Complete shared setup in the disposable profile. Use list_open_tabs to obtain the numeric id for the open https://example.org/ tab.

Warm/reload repetition: Warm run: obtain tab ID from list_open_tabs immediately before lookup. After extension, panel, and target reload, reacquire the ID from list_open_tabs before the second lookup.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
Run get_tab_info with {"tab_id":<numeric ID returned by list_open_tabs>}.
Compare returned id, URL, title, active/pinned state, status, and window_id against list_open_tabs and Chrome's tab strip.
Do not use an ID from a previous profile or earlier browser session.

After this warm pass, reload the extension, close/reopen Tools, and reload the target tab. Run list_open_tabs again to reacquire the current numeric tab ID, then rerun get_tab_info and compare current metadata.
expected: The returned record describes the same open target and its current state. No tab is changed.
A stale/unknown ID returns {ok:false,reason:<Chrome error>} and should be recorded as a stale-fixture input, not a successful lookup.
EXT-F-4038-T01.auth_notes: Inventory lists tabs permission; member/admin applicable. Manual run skips dispatcher permission gate.
limits: Use only IDs discovered in the current run; tab identifiers are ephemeral.

EXT-F-4039-T01.title: Search only synthetic public bookmarks in an isolated profile
preconditions: Complete shared setup. Prepare an isolated test profile with a small known set of bookmarks to public example.org URLs, including one titled 'Matrx public fixture alpha'; do not use the everyday profile.
Warm/reload repetition: Run in the same isolated profile before and after extension reload/Tools reopen; do not switch to an everyday profile.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
Run search_bookmarks with {"query":"Matrx public fixture alpha","limit":10}.
Compare returned count, total_match, title and URL with the single synthetic bookmark you created for this isolated test profile.
Run {"query":"zz-no-such-test-bookmark-zz","limit":10} to inspect the no-match response.
After this warm pass, reload the extension and reopen Tools, then rerun both bookmark queries in the same isolated profile and compare the known fixture bookmark and no-match response.
expected: The first result includes the synthetic bookmark and total_match reflects the full match count; count is capped at limit. The second returns zero matches. This tool only reads bookmarks.
An API-unavailable or permission error is visible and is not equivalent to an empty successful result. Do not expose bookmark data from other profiles in evidence.
EXT-F-4039-T01.auth_notes: Inventory lists bookmarks permission; member/admin applicable. Manual Run skips dispatcher permission checks; this is a read of profile-local personal data, restricted to the isolated fixture profile.
limits: Bookmark setup is a prerequisite performed only in a disposable profile; this proposed tool case itself is read-only. No real user bookmark should be surfaced or recorded.

EXT-F-4040-T01.title: Read the shallow tree of synthetic public bookmarks
preconditions: Complete shared setup. In the isolated profile, identify a test bookmark folder containing only public example.org URLs and record its folder ID; do not point at a personal profile's tree.

Warm/reload repetition: Run in the same isolated profile before and after extension reload/Tools reopen. If profile recreation changes folder IDs, reacquire the fixture folder ID before the second query.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
Run list_bookmark_tree with {"folder_id":"<isolated-test-folder-id>","max_depth":2}.
Inspect the returned tree for the known folder and fixture bookmark titles/URLs. Confirm traversal stops at the requested depth.
If testing default-root behavior, run {} only in this isolated profile and compare it to the small known fixture tree.

After this warm pass, reload the extension and reopen Tools, then rerun list_bookmark_tree with the same isolated folder ID and depth. If the profile was recreated, reacquire the folder ID from that profile before running.
expected: The result contains tree nodes with id/title/date_added and public URL values for bookmark nodes; child traversal is bounded by max_depth. The handler does not modify bookmarks.
A missing folder ID returns an explicit API error; do not substitute a guessed ID or treat an unrelated root as success.
EXT-F-4040-T01.auth_notes: Inventory lists bookmarks permission; member/admin applicable. Manual run bypasses dispatcher gate. Restrict use to the isolated synthetic profile because a full tree can reveal personal data.
limits: Tree shape depends on the browser's standard folders. Avoid asserting full root shape; use the isolated folder and exact synthetic entries.

EXT-F-4041-T01.title: Search known public visits in an isolated profile
preconditions: Complete shared setup in a disposable profile. Before seeding visits, record start_time_ms as the current Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds. Then visit https://example.org/ and https://example.org/?matrx-history-fixture=2 in that profile; do not use the everyday profile. Immediately before the first tool invocation, record end_time_ms as current Unix epoch milliseconds. Use those recorded numeric values in both query objects.
Warm/reload repetition: Run in the same isolated profile before and after extension reload/Tools reopen, reusing the recorded numeric time bounds exactly.
steps: Warm execution: perform this sequence once before any case-specific extension reload and record the inline results.

Run search_history with {"query":"example.org","start_time_ms":<recorded-numeric-start-ms>,"end_time_ms":<recorded-numeric-end-ms>,"max_results":100}. Both numeric bounds are Unix epoch milliseconds; start was recorded before seeding visits and end immediately before this invocation.
Inspect count/items; require the two seeded public URLs to appear with last_visit_ms between the recorded bounds.
Run the no-match query {"query":"zz-no-such-test-history-zz","start_time_ms":<same-recorded-start-ms>,"end_time_ms":<same-recorded-end-ms>,"max_results":100}.
After extension reload, reopen Tools and rerun both queries with the exact same numeric bounds; verify the seeded visits remain in-window and the sentinel query remains empty.
expected: The positive query returns the two seeded public-profile URLs within the explicitly recorded numeric millisecond interval and count equals items.length; the sentinel query returns no items matching its unique query. The tool itself does not navigate or change history.
A missing history capability/error is explicit. Do not interpret an empty positive result as success until the isolated profile's known visits and recorded bounds are confirmed.
EXT-F-4041-T01.auth_notes: Inventory lists history permission; member/admin applicable. Manual Run bypasses dispatcher gating. History is personal data, so run only in the disposable profile seeded with public targets; never inspect ordinary browsing history.
limits: Record start before visiting https://example.org/ and https://example.org/?matrx-history-fixture=2; record end immediately before the first query, both as Unix epoch milliseconds. Require those exact seeded URLs and in-window last_visit_ms values. Repeat with identical bounds after reload.

ambiguities_and_limits: Only the ten selected T01 cases are proposed here. Separate inventory access/permission negative cases and readiness gaps remain outstanding and must stay unchanged when root merges these procedure fields.
The Tools manual runner explicitly skips the permission gate. These cases cannot establish dispatcher authorization; gated/access cases require their own procedure and authorized execution path.
Catalog permissions and handler source may differ as catalog changes. Reconcile live catalog/registry before execution; manual runs cannot establish permission denial.
All procedures are design-only and remain unexecuted/unverified. No tests, browser, build, network, database, or app runs were performed.
